Logging calls

Source: vignettes/logging.Rmd
logging.Rmd
library(fnware)
library(S7)

log_call() logs when a call starts, and when it finishes or fails. Each message holds the function’s name, its arguments and, once the call is over, the time it took.

add := log_call() %@% function(a, b) a + b
add(1, b = 2)
## [1] 3

Arguments are named by the formals they matched, so add(b = 2, a = 1) logs the same as above. Long values are cut. A failure is logged and then signalled again unchanged:

boom := log_call() %@% function(x) stop("boom")
boom(1)
## Error:
## ! boom

Levels

Each event has a level. By default the start and the finish are info and a failure is error. Change them with log_levels():

quiet := log_call(
  logger = logger_message(),
  level = log_levels(start = "debug", finish = "debug", error = "warn")
) %@% function(x) stop("boom")
try(quiet(1), silent = TRUE)
## WARN [2026-11-10T20:40:01.230Z]: quiet(x=1) 
## Error in `quiet(x = x)`:
## boom

The start and finish are debug here, below the loggers’ default threshold of "info", so only the failure is written.

Set elapsed = FALSE to leave the time out of the finish message.

Traces

When a call fails, the calls from the decorated function down to the failure are logged as a separate trace event straight after the error. The built-in loggers only write events at or above their threshold, which is "info" by default, so the trace stays hidden until you lower it:

inner <- function(x) stop("boom")
outer := log_call(logger = logger_message(threshold = "trace")) %@%
  function(x) inner(x)
try(outer(1), silent = TRUE)
## INFO [2026-11-10T20:40:01.295Z]: Start outer(x=1)
## ERROR [2026-11-10T20:40:01.295Z]: outer(x=1) 
## Error in `inner(x)`:
## boom
## TRACE [2026-11-10T20:40:01.296Z]: outer(x=1) 
##   1. outer(x = x)
##   2. inner(x)
##   3. stop("boom")

Loggers

A logger decides where a message goes. logger_base(), the default, prints LEVEL [timestamp]: message. logger_message() writes the same line with message() instead, so suppressMessages() silences it. Both take a threshold, one of "trace", "debug", "info", "warn", "error" or "fatal", and leave out anything below it.

hello := log_call(logger = logger_message()) %@% function() "hi"
hello()
## INFO [2026-11-10T20:40:01.359Z]: Start hello()
## INFO [2026-11-10T20:40:01.360Z]: Finished hello() Elapsed=00:00:00.000
## [1] "hi"

Using a logging package

To log with another package, inherit from logger_base and add a method for logger_fn(). The package then owns thresholds, layouts and appenders. The method receives the level label ("INFO", "DEBUG" and so on) and the message, and decides for itself whether to show it, so threshold is not used.

For the logger package:

library(logger)
logger_logger := new_class(parent = logger_base)

method(logger_fn, logger_logger) <- function(class, level, msg, ...) {
  log_level(level, skip_formatter(msg))
}

f := log_call(logger = logger_logger()) %@% function(x) x
f(1)

skip_formatter() stops the logger package treating braces in the message as a glue template.

Some packages need a logger object passed in. Give it to the logger through the logger property and read it back as class@logger. For log4r:

library(log4r)
logger_log4r := new_class(parent = logger_base)

method(logger_fn, logger_log4r) <- function(class, level, msg, ...) {
  log_at(class@logger, level, msg)
}

f := log_call(logger = logger_log4r(logger = logger("INFO"))) %@%
  function(x) x
f(1)

If a package names its levels differently, override the defaults of the trace, debug, info, warn, error and fatal properties. A label can be any object, for example a number.

logger_num := new_class(
  parent = logger_base,
  properties = list(
    info = new_property(class_any, default = 20L),
    debug = new_property(class_any, default = 10L)
  )
)

method(logger_fn, logger_num) <- function(class, level, msg, ...) {
  cat(level, msg, "\n")
}

f := log_call(logger = logger_num()) %@% function() 1
f()
## 20 Start f() 
## 20 Finished f() Elapsed=00:00:00.000
## [1] 1

Promises

log_call() logs the finish as soon as the function returns, which for a function that returns a promise is before the work is done. Use async_log_call() instead. It logs the start when the function is called, and the finish or the failure when the promise settles. A rejection is logged then passed on unchanged. It logs no trace event, because the calls that led to a rejection are gone by the time it settles.

f := async_log_call(logger = logger_message()) %@%
  function(x) promises::promise_resolve(x)
promises::then(f(1), print)
